verdict_reason: The formula is Rudman et al. 2022 Eq. 4.1 exactly. On EXACT k-of-9 clouds (orthonormalised so the covariance spectrum is exactly k ones and 9-k zeros, then rotated) BLME reproduces the paper's Table 2 closed form iota(I_9^(k)) = (k-1)/8 at k = 1..9 with worst absolute error 2.220e-16, and against the released IsoScore 2.0.1 package executed locally on six clouds (isotropic 1000x8 and 500x64, the N<d 20x100 branch, anisotropic 300x16, rank-3 400x12, clustered 600x32) the worst ABSOLUTE disagreement is 3.031e-08. The round-3/4 scale defect is closed. YELLOW is for ONE value-changing counterexample that the released package does NOT have. IsoScore is translation-invariant by construction -- it is a function of the covariance -- but isotropy.py:264 does `np.asarray(X - X.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True), dtype=np.float64)`, computing the mean AND the subtraction in the INPUT dtype and only then promoting. On a float32 4096x8 exactly-balanced integer cloud translated by +1,000,000 -- a translation that is exactly representable and exactly recoverable (`(X+1e6)-1e6 == X` bit for bit) -- BLME returns 0.001783276461 where the released IsoScore 2.0.1 returns 0.995837092400 and BLME's own untranslated value is 0.995837039632: a -99.82% error. Promoting X to float64 BEFORE the mean restores it exactly (0.995837039632 at offsets 1e6 and 1e7). This is the same defect class rounds 2-4 removed from thirteen other tasks, applied to translation rather than scale, and it is the last uncorrected site I found in this task. ADJUDICATION: where the two round-4 reviewers disagreed, my measurement supports gpt-5.6-sol. Its translated-cloud counterexample REPRODUCES independently here (BLME 0.001783276461 vs official 0.995837092400) and the round-4 Opus GREEN, which tested only scale and not translation, missed it.
comparable_reason: Raw `isoscore` carries an exact structural 1/(d-1) factor, so a model that genuinely uses k dimensions scores lower simply for being wider. Direct intervention: a fixed rank-8 cloud zero-padded from d = 64 to 4096 -- an exact isometry that changes nothing about the geometry -- moves the raw score 0.110927321 -> 0.027405573 -> 0.006831301 -> 0.001706574, a factor of 65. Across the 61 archived study models whose config I could resolve, raw isoscore has Spearman -0.4164 with d_model (p = 8.4e-4), -0.3146 with n_layers (p = 0.014), -0.4397 with vocab_size (p = 3.9e-4) and -0.4623 with log_params (p = 1.8e-4). Only `isoscore_effective_dims` should enter a cross-width feature matrix -- and note that it is the SAME quantity as geometry_svd's `participation_ratio`, so the two must not both be used as independent features.
github_reason: Read the released `IsoScore.IsoScore` source (torch.cov -> torch.linalg.svdvals -> pcs*sqrt(n)/||pcs|| -> defect/sqrt(2(n-sqrt n)) -> the Eq. 4.1 rescale) and ran it head to head with BLME's `_isoscore` on six float64 clouds: worst absolute disagreement 3.031e-08 (isotropic 3.19e-10 and 6.57e-09, N<d 2.00e-08, anisotropic 3.03e-08, rank-3 6.83e-09, clustered 2.15e-08). I then used the same package as the arbiter for the translation counterexample: at a float32 +1e6 offset it stays at 0.995837092400 across offsets 0, 1e5, 1e6 and 1e7 while BLME drops to 0.001783276461, so the divergence is BLME's arithmetic and not a definitional disagreement.
paper_reason: Rudman et al. (arXiv:2108.07344) Table 2 publishes iota(I_9^(k)) = (k-1)/8 for k = 1..9, i.e. 0.000, 0.125, 0.250, 0.375, 0.500, 0.625, 0.750, 0.875, 1.000. Driving exact k-of-9 clouds (SVD-orthonormalised to a spectrum of exactly k ones, then randomly rotated) through BLME's kernel returns 0.000000000000000, 0.125000000000000, 0.250000000000000, 0.375000000000000, 0.500000000000000, 0.625000000000000, 0.750000000000000, 0.875000000000000, 1.000000000000000 -- worst absolute error 2.220e-16, i.e. all nine published values to machine precision.
confounds_reason: For the RAW score the confound is confirmed and its mechanism is known exactly: it is the 1/(d-1) factor in Eq. 4.1, demonstrated by a zero-padding isometry that moves the score 65x (0.110927321 at d=64 -> 0.001706574 at d=4096) with the geometry held fixed, and by Spearman -0.4164 with d_model / -0.4623 with log_params over 61 archived models. The ambient-corrected twin removes it: rho(d_model) -0.4164 -> -0.0712 (p = 0.585), rho(n_layers) -0.3146 -> -0.0419 (p = 0.748), rho(log_params) -0.4623 -> -0.1380 (p = 0.289). The one channel the twin does NOT remove is vocabulary: rho(vocab_size) goes -0.4397 -> -0.4837 (p = 7.9e-5). Vocabulary is essentially a model-family label in this zoo (50k GPT-2 / 128k Llama / 152k Qwen / 256k Gemma), and the association is present in the raw score too, so this is not the twin relocating a width effect -- but it is a family-level association that survives the correction and should be stated.
defects: CODE, VALUE-CHANGING isotropy.py:264: `Xc = np.asarray(X - X.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True), dtype=np.float64)` computes the mean AND the subtraction in the INPUT dtype and only then promotes. IsoScore is translation-invariant by definition and the released package is; BLME is not. Float32 4096x8 balanced integer cloud translated by +1e6 (exactly representable, `(X+1e6)-1e6 == X` bit for bit): BLME 0.001783276461 against the official 0.995837092400 and BLME's own untranslated 0.995837039632, -99.82%. Verified LATENT on real data -- on 8,384 gpt2 last-layer states the float32 path agrees with a float64 reference to rel -2.402e-09 -- but the headroom is only about 50x: the largest per-column |mean|/std is 158.26 (max |mean| 196.52), and an added offset of 1e4 already moves the value +0.76%, 1e5 gives +139%, 1e6 gives -98.7%. Fix: `X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)` BEFORE the mean, which is a no-op at offset 0 (0.995837039632 either way) and restores exactness at 1e6 and 1e7.
